requirement: Python applications shall be able to submit function evaluations for asynchronous execution, wait for all child tasks or a selected task collection, and retrieve completed tasks in completion order. Each task shall make its submitted inputs and computed return value available to the application.

Applications shall be able to associate a callback with a submitted task. After the task completes and its results return, the callback shall run on the MPI process that submitted the task and receive the completed task descriptor, including access to its input and result.

The library shall support parallel application of a function over one or more input sequences, with configurable chunk sizes and an ordered list of results. Applications shall also be able to express nested parallel tasks and loops.

The library shall distribute tasks cyclically across available workers by default and allow applications to direct a task to a specified worker queue, rejecting invalid worker identifiers. Applications shall be able to enable or disable inter-process task stealing. When it is enabled, idle workers with empty queues shall be able to retrieve pending tasks from other MPI processes for execution.

The library shall provide a common Python task execution model for shared-memory and distributed-memory environments, using MPI with mpi4py and Python worker threads. Applications shall be able to initialize the runtime, launch a primary application task on MPI rank 0, and shut down the runtime. They shall also be able to switch between task-parallel and SPMD execution, running a specified function on all MPI processes and invoking application-level MPI routines without managing the library's internal communication.
Applications shall be able to obtain the current worker identifier, total worker count, current MPI rank, and total MPI process count, and obtain time values for measuring execution duration.

Users shall be able to configure the number of worker threads per MPI process, whether inter-process task stealing is enabled, and idle-yield timing for server and worker threads through environment variables. The default configuration shall use one worker thread per MPI process with task stealing disabled.
